messages:
maria: Heads up — customer-reported intermittent cross-org rows in the Console after a rapid org switch. saw it twice in a row on prod just now.
raj: ugh. can you paste what the UI showed? screenshot or console logs?
tess: I saw something similar yesterday in staging when running the fast-switch webdriver test. the list preview stuttered and briefly showed names from the previous org.
maria: screenshot: (cropped) shows org B rows while header says org A. also in network tab the /api/internal/preview returned 200 with body containing other_org_id.
raj: logs from the gateway around the time: ```INFO fetchPreview user=alice org=org-A route=/preview id=xyz cache_key=org-A|preview|xyz
INFO fetchPreview cache_miss route=/preview backend=console-service```
raj: then console-service log: ```DEBUG hydratePreview user=alice org=org-A resolved_workspace=org-A
DEBUG loadPanel -> rows fetched from cache key=org-B|panel|123```
raj: that cache key is the smoking gun — somehow cache key mixed org-B in console-service.
tess: suspecting the prefetch path (fast-switch prefetch) that races: prefetch for org-B completes while the request context is already switched to org-A and we stash the result without rekeying.
maria: repro steps I used: rapidly click org switch 3x within 0.5s, open the dashboard, see mixed rows ~20% of runs. seems timing dependent.
raj: can we confirm where the cache key is composed? is it coming from upstream header X-Org or from internal route param?
tess: code pointer: console-service/src/cache/keys.go where buildKey uses ctx.Org or header fallback. quick patch I tried: enforce `org := ctx.Org; if org == "" {org = req.Header.Get("x-org-id")}` but we might be losing ctx.Org on race.
raj: hunch: context object mutated by goroutine doing prefetch. we have a shared mutable request-scoped state.
ess: (typo) meant tess. :facepalm:
maria: infra-bot: deploy log? any rolling update around 12:03?
infra-bot: deploy-bot: new deploy console-service v2.14.1 completed at 2026-02-15T12:02:58Z (sha: a1b2c3). no restarts after.
raj: timeline lines up; but this sounds like a logical race introduced earlier. can someone run local repro with the race detector or add logging to cache key build to print goroutine id and request id?
tess: I'll add verbose trace logs to print req.id, ctx.org, header.x-org and cache_key before write. also add a small mutex around cache write as quick mitigation for canary.
maria: mitigation plan: 1) enable verbose canary logging on 10% of requests; 2) push a guarded cache-write middleware (mutex per key namespace) for canary; 3) block rollouts to more customers until we confirm.
raj: we should also add a server-side assertion: before returning preview check that response.org == request.org and drop if mismatch (fail open with 500) — that will avoid leaking other org rows to clients.
tess: agree. adding the assertion is cheap and safe for now. will open PR with tests and repro harness.
maria: please tag me on PR. also need a KB entry for support describing the temporary mitigation (canary & assertion).
raj: long-term: audit all places using request-context mutation and prefetch goroutines. prefer immutable request-scoped structs or copy-on-write.
maria: reassigning to eng-platform triage to track until fixed. thanks all. :thumbsup:
